tagline: Leader in data center AI and high-performance computing
hero_kpi_rationale: Data center revenue is AMD's primary growth driver, fueled by strong demand for AI and server chips with 5th generation EPYC processors and Instinct MI350 GPUs, positioning AMD as a direct challenger to Nvidia in the generative AI wave.

kpis.name: Data Center Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by processors and GPUs for data centers, primarily used in AI and cloud computing.
kpis.description: In 2025, the data center segment generated $16.6 billion in revenue, up 32% from $12.6 billion in 2024, driven by strong demand for 5th generation AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs.
kpis.signal: Strong growth driven by AI and hyperscaler demand.

kpis.name: HPC and Cloud Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue tied to high-performance computing and AI solutions, included within data center segment, key for future growth.
kpis.description: AI and HPC revenue is included in the data center segment, which reached $16.6 billion in 2025, driven by Instinct GPUs dedicated to generative AI workloads.
kpis.signal: AMD captures AI wave through data center GPU momentum.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total sales realized by AMD across all segments during the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Total net revenue reached $34.6 billion in 2025, compared to $25.8 billion in 2024, representing 34% year-over-year growth driven by data center and client/gaming segments.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deduction of cost of goods sold and amortization of acquisition-related intangibles.
kpis.description: Gross margin improved to 50.0% in 2025 from 49.3% in 2024, primarily due to favorable product mix, partially offset by approximately $440 million of net inventory and related charges associated with U.S. government export controls on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products.
kpis.signal: Stable and elevated gross margin despite export control inventory charges.

kpis.name: R&D Intensity
kpis.explanation: R&D spending as a percentage of net revenue, reflecting investment in AI and new product development.
kpis.description: R&D expenses reached $8.091 billion in 2025, representing 23.4% of net revenue, compared to $6.456 billion or 25.0% in 2024, reflecting disciplined investment in AI and product roadmaps.
kpis.signal: Significant R&D investment for AI advancement and next-generation products.

kpis.name: Capex Intensity
kpis.explanation: Ratio of capital expenditures to net revenue, reflecting moderate capex requirements of fabless business model.
kpis.description: Capital expenditures totaled $974 million in 2025, representing 2.8% of net revenue, compared to $645 million or 2.5% in 2024, supporting capacity expansion and infrastructure investments.
kpis.signal: Moderate capex reflecting fabless business model with outsourced manufacturing.

kpis.name: Inventory Days
kpis.explanation: Number of days of inventory on hand for finished goods and components.
kpis.description: Inventory days increased to 102 days in 2025 from 90 days in 2024, reflecting a buildup related to anticipated AI demand and impact of U.S. export control charges on MI308 products.
kpis.signal: Inventory buildup reflecting demand preparation and export control impacts.

kpis.name: Client and Gaming Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from Ryzen processors, Radeon GPUs and semi-custom SoCs for gaming consoles and PCs.
kpis.description: The Client and Gaming segment revenue increased to $14.6 billion in 2025 from $9.6 billion in 2024, driven by strong demand for AMD Ryzen processors, Radeon 9000 Series GPUs, and semi-custom SoCs for game consoles.
kpis.signal: Major rebound in gaming and PC markets.

kpis.name: Embedded Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from embedded processors for industrial and networking applications.
kpis.description: Embedded segment revenue declined 3% to $3.5 billion in 2025 from $3.6 billion in 2024, as certain end market demand remained mixed across industrial and networking verticals.
kpis.signal: Slight decline due to mixed demand across end markets.

ai_positioning.summary: AMD positions itself as a leader in AI with a comprehensive vertical strategy encompassing hardware, software, and strategic partnerships. Through its Instinct GPU lineup, ROCm software ecosystem, and major agreements with OpenAI and Meta, AMD is accelerating penetration into the generative AI market.
evidence: Launch of AMD Instinct MI350 Series and MI450 Series GPUs dedicated to AI workloads with annual cadence
Strategic partnership with OpenAI: 6 GW GPU deployment agreement with MI450 series as first deployment, warrant for 160M shares at $0.01

Acquisition of ZT Systems for AI infrastructure design capabilities and related technology assets; software ecosystem expansion through targeted acquisitions in compiler, machine learning, photonics, and AI inference
ROCm software stack optimization for generative AI workloads with expanded framework support
